text:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert - Dedicated VPC canary failures for customer HeliosHealth in eu-west-1. Elevated 5xx rate on canary instances in pool `helios-dedicated-eu1`. Error: kernel mismatch / model load failures. Pager to oncall.
amanda_ng: ack. I'm oncall for infra, taking lead. @sanjay_patel if you can stand by for routing/fallback help.
emily_tsai: support FYI — HeliosHealth reported some 500s show up in their telemetry, they see a small fraction of requests failing. They're asking for ETA.
amanda_ng: quick impact note: canary traffic is ~3% of HeliosHealth's requests. Non-canary traffic appears healthy. We'll keep customer in the loop.
ops-bot: Canary group `helios-canary-2026-03` health: 60% healthy, 40% failing. Recent failures: `LD_PRELOAD` mismatch and KernelVersion errors. Rolling artifacts: `rwinf/serve:v2.3.1-quant` deployed to canary.
sanjay_patel: likely regression from runtime kernel selection in v2.3.1. Suggest pinning canary to v2.3.0 and pausing rollout. Also consider immediate rollback of canary group only.
amanda_ng: plan proposal:
1) pause rollout for HeliosHealth (control-plane)
2) pin canary pool to previously stable artifact v2.3.0
3) scale down canary group and shift canary traffic to stable nodes
4) monitor for 15m then communicate rollback complete to customer
amanda_ng: commands to pause rollout and pin artifact (control-plane CLI):

```
rictl rollout pause --tenant helioshealth --pool helios-dedicated-eu1 --rollout-id helios-canary-2026-03
rictl artifact pin --tenant helioshealth --pool helios-dedicated-eu1 --artifact rwinf/serve:v2.3.0
rictl pool scale --tenant helioshealth --pool helios-dedicated-eu1 --canary-count 0
```

amanda_ng: executing step 1 now.
ops-bot: action log: rollout paused by amanda_ng at 1750001220
amanda_ng: pinning artifact now.
ops-bot: artifact pin command accepted. previous pin rwinf/serve:v2.3.0 restored at 1750001287
derek_hsu: on infra infra-side, I'm going to reduce canary instances gracefully and drain existing ones.
amanda_ng: runbook drain command:

```
rictl node drain --tenant helioshealth --node <node-id>
# then
rictl pool scale --tenant helioshealth --pool helios-dedicated-eu1 --canary-count 0
```

derek_hsu: starting drain. Draining nodes: node-eu1-47, node-eu1-48
ops-bot: node-eu1-47 drain started (1750001440)
ops-bot: node-eu1-48 drain started (1750001465)

rachel_support: @emily_tsai pls send a short note to HeliosHealth: "We paused the canary rollout and restored the previous artifact. You may see transient retries; majority of traffic should be served normally." I'll take customer comms once state stabilizes.
emily_tsai: on it. Draft: "Hi — we've paused a canary rollout affecting a small portion of your traffic to investigate 5xxs. We've restored the previous artifact and are draining canary instances. We'll update in 15 minutes."
pm-olga: are we sure this is artifact-related and not a VPC-level kernel upgrade? we saw kernel mismatch errors earlier.
julia_eng_infra: logs show loader errors referencing quantized ops in v2.3.1 that were compiled against a newer CUDA patch level not present on some dedicated nodes.
sanjay_patel: that matches. Some dedicated nodes in that pool are running an older AMI. Short-term mitigation is pinning artifact + draining. Long-term: we need node compatibility gating in rollout.
amanda_ng: monitor window starting. Metrics to watch: 5xx rate on tenant, successful model loads, node OOMs, CPU spikes.

```
# quick queries
rictl metrics tenant helioshealth --window 5m --metric http_5xx_rate
rictl logs tenant helioshealth --filter "model_load_error" --since 10m
```

ops-bot: metrics: tenant helioshealth 5xx rate dropped from 3.2% -> 0.4% after pin and drains (1750001900)
derek_hsu: can confirm canary nodes are drained to 0. No ongoing active requests on canary fleet.
amanda_ng: great. I'll mark mitigation in incident tracker and prepare for handoff.

incident-bot: Incident HeliosHealth-dedicated-canary | mitigated -> monitoring | severity downgraded to SEV3 (1750002200)

emily_tsai: customer update sent: "We've paused the canary rollout and rolled back the canary to the previous artifact. We see error rates falling and are continuing to monitor. We'll follow up with a postmortem and next steps to prevent recurrence." Customer replied: "Thanks — please keep us posted. No major impact on our users so far."
sanjay_patel: follow-ups (owner: eng-infra):
- add AMI/driver compatibility check to rollout preflight
- add rollout gating to prevent cross-AMI canaries
- create alert for mixed-kernel nodes in a single pool

amanda_ng: handoff to oncall for next shift: @derek_hsu you're the follow-up owner for 24h. Please keep watch and coordinate any re-rollout windows with PM/CS.
derek_hsu: ack. I'll own follow-ups and schedule a brief postmortem with eng-infra + release team. Putting notes in incident tracker.

rachel_support: I'll coordinate a customer postmortem invite with HeliosHealth CSM.
pm-olga: thanks everyone. small ask: include the pinned-artifact id and node ids in postmortem.

amanda_ng: final note: mitigation successful, canary rollback completed, customer minimally impacted. Creating follow-up ticket for gating and automation. :thumbsup:
sanjay_patel: :eyes:
incident-bot: thread closed (1750005311)"
